Coming in Hot

AI Tools of the Week

  1. 🤖 Symphony builds you a team of AI agents, loaded with wisdom from 300M small businesses like yours. Grow faster. Run further.

  2. 🔍 Are You Found By AI scans 7 AI engines for what they say about your business, quoting every answer word for word and flagging name mix-ups.

  3. 🦅 ChatHawk sends one question to GPT, Gemini, Claude, and Grok at once, then merges the answers and shows you where they agree and where they split.

  4. 🎬 Movie Maker Edit Pro turns a folder of AI clips into a finished film, ordering shots, setting transitions, rendering, and leveling the sound on its own.

  5. 📐 MathBuddy solves math from algebra to multivariable calculus, showing the rule behind every step and generating a short whiteboard video when the steps still confuse you.

  6. 📈 Rankora runs keyword research, daily rank tracking, and site audits from one dashboard, covering both classic search results and the AI answers people read instead.

  7. 🎬 IdeaVideo holds one character, product, or style steady across every shot, so a single idea becomes a finished video instead of scattered clips.

  8. 🎵 Yinso turns lyrics or a rough idea into a finished song across disco, jazz, lo-fi, and more, then splits the track into editable stems.

  9. 🐱 CatDoes rebuilds any WordPress, Shopify, or Lovable site as a native mobile app, and runs its own cloud computer to fix its own errors.

  10. 🛍️ Anyvids shoots your product catalog with AI, generating photos and video, relighting scenes, and running virtual try-on so nothing needs a studio.

 

🦾 Launch your AI tool on the #1 AI tools marketplace.

 
 
 
Interesting AI

This Week’s Most Interesting AI

A dog named Rosie was out of options. Surgery, chemo, and immunotherapy had all failed, and the vets gave her months.

Gamgee builds a cancer vaccine out of the dog’s own tumor. Sequence the tumor, compare it against healthy blood, and the mutations unique to the cancer show up. Software ranks which ones are worth attacking, trained on dog biology rather than human. Those become an mRNA shot that hands the immune system a target list. Her owner ran the first one himself, after 17 years in machine learning. Several of Rosie’s tumors shrank.

That first attempt took a year. It now runs as a clinical trial in Australia, four weeks from biopsy to a vaccine in the vet’s hands.
